laws.rule: In the City of Cork it is an offence to drink alcohol on a street or in a public place (open spaces, river banks, parks and green spaces) in the council's area. It is also an offence to hold alcohol in an opened can, opened bottle, opened pack or a glass or cup while on a street or in an open space intending to drink it there; the bye-laws presume that intent unless the person shows otherwise. The fine on conviction in the District Court is up to EUR 2,500 (about A$3,973 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) (Cork City Council bye-laws, paragraphs 2 to 4, as commenced in January 2022). Drinking at tables and chairs a hotel, restaurant or pub provides next to it, within its licence and licensed hours, is not an offence (paragraph 5). Any member of the Garda is an authorised person.

laws.rule: The Cork County Council (Regulation and Control of Certain Beaches) Bye-laws 2011 apply during the summer season (15 May to 31 August) to the 45 beaches listed in Schedule 1, including Harbour View at Kilbrittain, Coolmain, Sandycove, Garrettstown and Garrylucas near Kinsale, Fountainstown, Claycastle, Pilmore and Redbarn at Youghal, Inchydoney, Barley Cove, Tragumna, Ownahincha, Courtmacsherry, Myrtleville and Fennells Bay at Crosshaven. The official 2011 text applies in the county functional area excluding the then towns of Youghal, Cobh, Midleton, Kinsale, Macroom, Skibbereen, Clonakilty, Mallow and Fermoy. On the scheduled beaches it is forbidden to disobey an authorised person, lifeguard or member of An Garda Siochana, damage dunes or vegetation, cause a nuisance, play sports with high-speed projectiles such as golf or archery, use quad bikes in the dunes, sell or hire goods or offer paid water-sports tuition without consent or a permit, light an open fire (other than in a contained unit such as a barbecue), remove sand, stones, seaweed or soil without consent, camp or bring a caravan, camper or tent without consent, or drive or park a motor vehicle on the beach except in a designated area or with consent. Dogs must be on a leash between 12 pm and 6 pm and under effective control at all other times, with faeces removed. Horses must not be ridden or brought into a designated swimming area or a beach-guard controlled area between 11 am and 7 pm; riding must be below the mean high water mark except for access, and horses are not allowed on the dunes without consent. Launching recreational craft or personal watercraft is prohibited on the Schedule 1 beaches except at council-designated access points, and their use within 300 metres seaward of the water's edge is prohibited except for rescue or designated access; launching is also prohibited on inner Clonakilty Bay (Schedule 2). A person who contravenes the bye-laws is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding 1500 (the 2011 official text does not show a currency symbol in the extracted PDF). A fixed payment of 75 may be offered as an alternative to prosecution if paid within 21 days.
